sourceChecks.claim: Previously live-inspected Azure asynchronous request-reply for accepted job/status versus completed result and terminal errors; same claims apply to this export workflow.

Live inspected RabbitMQ acknowledgement boundaries: confirms cover producer/broker and are unaware of consumers; consumer ack permits retiring delivery. Neither coordinates arbitrary database effects.

Live inspected AWS idempotent APIs: caller intent identifier reused on retries and recording token plus mutating effect must form an ACID operation, avoiding either crash gap. RabbitMQ unacknowledged redelivery gives the stated failure window.

Live inspected Azure Retry: cancel persistent faults, delay transient retries with finite count. Competing Consumers and Load Leveling explicitly isolate poison/exhausted messages for inspection and resubmission.

Live inspected Competing Consumers sequencing limitations and session-based ordering; concurrent receipt alone cannot serialize effects. The supplied two-write trace verifies the overwrite, and holding dependent work preserves the proposed lane rule.

Live inspected Queue-Based Load Leveling: bound aggregate downstream work, sustained producer excess grows queue/latency, shed producer work, respect finite quotas and retention. Stated arithmetic is correct.

Live inspected Kafka consumer position and delivery semantics: independent groups share partitions internally, rewind offsets while retained, progress separate from retention; external exactly-once needs output-system cooperation.

Previously live-inspected Azure asynchronous request-reply scope and costs; dependency on a completed authorization result makes synchronous acceptance necessary here. Deferred work requires observable terminal outcomes.
